task: 512-d face embedding (MobileFaceNet, MNET_V2). Not a detection/classification model - see uniface-adaface-recognition/manifest.json for the full explanation of why this manifest's shape differs from the intern-* manifests and what an embedding manifest can honestly claim.
note:
Real gate-2 shape independently re-confirmed this session: input 'input' FIXED (1,3,112,112) float32 (not a dynamic batch dimension like adaface/edgeface - confirmed live, matches CHECKLIST.md's prior write-up), output 'output' (1,512) float32. The fixed batch=1 means this engine (like sphereface below) only ever runs one aligned face crop per session.run call - already how UnifaceEmbeddingEngine.embed() calls it (one crop in, one embedding out), so no code change was needed for the fixed-batch case, but it is worth recording that the two fixed-batch models were not blindly assumed to behave like the two dynamic-batch ones.

Same fixture, same detector, same honesty caveats as uniface-adaface-recognition/manifest.json: only stock_streetscene_3adults.jpg has usable real faces anywhere in this repo's fixtures, the production SCRFD detector found 2 of the 3 visible faces, and there is no same-identity pair anywhere in this project's fixtures to test true recognition recall against.

MobileFace does not override BaseRecognizer.preprocess (confirmed against the real uniface/recognition/mobileface.py source) - RGB-converting, (pixel-127.5)/127.5 path, same as EdgeFace/SphereFace. Raw output on these two real faces is NOT unit-norm (1.77 / 1.95).

expected.non_degenerate: the two faces' embeddings must not be identical or all-zero
expected.different_identity_cosine_similarity_low: expected roughly near 0 (weak signal only, see uniface-adaface-recognition/manifest.json) for these two different real people
